question.problem: If $u=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ k \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ -8 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal vectors, then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =(-5)\cdot (-3)+k\cdot (-1)+2\cdot (-8)+(-6)\cdot 1 \\  & =15-k-16-6 \\  & =-k-7\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-k-7 & =0 \\ k & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$
